questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both a wind instrument and a tree?
explanation: Reed is correct - R-E-E-D. Reed is a homograph meaning both a tall grass plant and a vibrating strip in a wind instrument.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both to rest and the remainder?
explanation: Rest is correct - R-E-S-T. Rest is a homograph meaning to relax and the rest meaning the remaining part.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both a type of plant and to annoy?
explanation: Nettle is correct - N-E-T-T-L-E. Nettle is a homograph meaning the stinging plant and to nettle means to irritate.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word meaning both to look at and a timepiece?
explanation: Watch is correct - W-A-T-C-H. Watch is a homograph meaning to observe and also a wrist or pocket timepiece.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both a type of tree and a tool?
explanation: Plane is correct - P-L-A-N-E. Plane is a homograph for a type of tree an aeroplane and a tool for smoothing wood.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both a type of metal and to push?
explanation: Steel is correct - S-T-E-E-L. Steel means the metal alloy. To steel oneself means to prepare mentally. These are homographs.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both a rank and to row?
explanation: Rank is correct - R-A-N-K. Rank is a homograph meaning a position in a hierarchy and also meaning to have an unpleasant smell.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that can mean both to bow and a weapon for arrows?
explanation: Bow is correct - B-O-W. Bow is a heteronym. When it rhymes with go it means the weapon for arrows. When it rhymes with cow it means to bend forward.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that can mean both a period of time and to faint?
explanation: Spell is correct - S-P-E-L-L. Spell is a homograph meaning a period of time a magical incantation and to write letters in order.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both a test and a court examination?
explanation: Trial is correct - T-R-I-A-L. Trial is a homograph meaning a test and a formal legal examination of evidence.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that means either to record or a musical note?
explanation: Note is correct - N-O-T-E. Note is a homograph meaning a musical sound a written record and a currency denomination.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both a sharp point and a bar of metal?
explanation: Spike is correct - S-P-I-K-E. Spike is a homograph meaning a sharp point an increase and to add an ingredient to a drink.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that when stressed on first syllable means rubbish?
explanation: Refuse is correct - R-E-F-U-S-E. Refuse is a heteronym. Stressed on the first syllable it means rubbish. Stressed on second it means to decline.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that when stressed on first syllable means a document?
explanation: Record is correct - R-E-C-O-R-D. Record is a heteronym. Stressed on the first syllable it is a noun meaning a document. Stressed on the second it is a verb meaning to document.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that when stressed on first syllable means a conflict?
explanation: Conflict is correct - C-O-N-F-L-I-C-T. Conflict stressed on the first syllable is a noun. Stressed on the second it is a verb meaning to clash.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both to cook in an oven and a type of kiln?
explanation: Bake is correct - B-A-K-E. Bake means to cook by dry heat. A bake is also a homograph meaning a kiln used in pottery.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that means both a kind of protest and an object?
explanation: Object is correct - O-B-J-E-C-T. Object stressed on the first syllable is a noun meaning a thing. Stressed on the second it means to protest.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym meaning both a forward movement and an advance payment?
explanation: Advance is correct - A-D-V-A-N-C-E. Advance is a homograph meaning to move forward and also a payment made before it is due.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym meaning both to challenge and a type of deer?
explanation: Buck is correct - B-U-C-K. Buck is a homograph meaning a male deer currency and to challenge something.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that means both to flow and a steady motion?
explanation: Current is correct - C-U-R-R-E-N-T. Double R. Current is a homograph meaning a flow of water or electricity and also meaning happening now.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both a fault and a geographical feature?
explanation: Fault is correct - F-A-U-L-T. Fault is a homograph meaning a mistake and a break in rock strata in geology.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym where stress changes its meaning completely?
explanation: Produce is correct - P-R-O-D-U-C-E. Stressed on the first syllable it means farm goods as a noun. Stressed on the second it means to make as a verb.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym where stress changes its meaning from a gap to perforate?
explanation: Puncture is correct - P-U-N-C-T-U-R-E. Puncture is a homograph meaning a small hole and the act of piercing something.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word meaning both a type of grain and a texture?
explanation: Grain is correct - G-R-A-I-N. Grain is a homograph meaning a cereal crop and the texture or pattern of wood or fabric.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that can mean to put in a box or a sport?
explanation: Box is correct - B-O-X. Box is a homograph meaning a container a sport and the act of putting things in containers.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that can mean a type of fish or a type of metal?
explanation: Bass is correct - B-A-S-S. Bass is a heteronym. When it rhymes with face it means a type of fish. When it rhymes with race it means the lowest musical pitch.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that means both to shed and to throw light?
explanation: Shed is correct - S-H-E-D. Shed is a homograph meaning a small building to lose hair and to throw light on something.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that means both to look over and miss seeing?
explanation: Overlook is correct - O-V-E-R-L-O-O-K. Overlook is a homograph meaning to look at something from above and to fail to notice.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that means both a place for farming and to till soil?
explanation: Farm is correct - F-A-R-M. Farm is a homograph meaning a piece of agricultural land and to cultivate the land.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that can mean a musical key or a computer button?
explanation: Key is correct - K-E-Y. Key is a homograph meaning an instrument that opens a lock a musical note and a computer button.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both to guide and a poisonous metal?
explanation: Lead is correct - L-E-A-D. Lead is a heteronym. When it rhymes with need it means to guide. When it rhymes with bed it means the heavy metal.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that when stressed on first syllable means a present?
explanation: Present is correct - P-R-E-S-E-N-T. Stressed on the first syllable present is a noun meaning a gift. Stressed on the second it means to give or show.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that means both a row and a quarrel?
explanation: Row is correct - R-O-W. Row is a heteronym. When it rhymes with go it means a line. When it rhymes with cow it means a noisy argument.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that can mean tears or to rip?
explanation: Tear is correct - T-E-A-R. Tear is a heteronym. When it rhymes with ear it means a drop from the eye. When it rhymes with bare it means to rip.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that means both a type of tree and to give up?
explanation: Resign is correct - R-E-S-I-G-N. Resign as one word means to give up a position. Re-sign hyphenated means to sign again. The G is silent.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that means both to wound and a result?
explanation: Wound is correct - W-O-U-N-D. Wound is a heteronym. When it rhymes with moon it means an injury. When it rhymes withound it means wrapped around.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both a type of plant and a container?
explanation: Bulb is correct - B-U-L-B. Bulb is a homograph meaning a plant corm a light bulb and the rounded part of a thermometer.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that changes meaning based on stress: project or to throw forward?
explanation: Project is correct - P-R-O-J-E-C-T. Stressed on the first syllable it is a noun. Stressed on the second syllable it means to throw forward or predict.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both a measure of land and a scheme?
explanation: Plot is correct - P-L-O-T. Plot is a homograph meaning a piece of land the main story of a book and to scheme secretly.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both to hit and a clock sound?
explanation: Strike is correct - S-T-R-I-K-E. Strike is a homograph meaning to hit a workers protest a bowling term and the sound of a clock striking.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both a young dog and a type of seal?
explanation: Pup is correct - P-U-P. Pup is a homograph meaning a young dog and a young seal. It is also informal for a cheeky young person.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym meaning either to permit or a golf count?
explanation: Allow is correct - A-L-L-O-W. Allow means to permit something. Double L. It is also a homograph used in the term allowance.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word that means both to stop and a pause in music?
explanation: Rest is correct - R-E-S-T. Rest is a homograph meaning a pause a musical pause and the remaining part.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym where the noun means a type of metal and the verb means to iron?
explanation: Iron is correct - I-R-O-N. Iron is a homograph meaning the metal and to smooth clothes with a heated device.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word meaning both a race event and running smoothly?
explanation: Run is correct - R-U-N. Run is a homograph with meanings including to move quickly a run in tights and a period of operation.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word meaning both a flat surface and to organise?
explanation: Level is correct - L-E-V-E-L. Level is a homograph meaning a flat surface a tool for measuring horizontal surfaces and to knock down.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word meaning both to type and a category?
explanation: Type is correct - T-Y-P-E. Type is a homograph meaning a category of thing and to write using a keyboard.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word meaning both a letter of the alphabet and a grade?
explanation: Grade is correct - G-R-A-D-E. Grade is a homograph meaning a level of quality a school year and a mark or score.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the heteronym that changes meaning based on syllable stress - from a noun to increase?
explanation: Increase is correct - I-N-C-R-E-A-S-E. Stressed on the first syllable it is a noun meaning a rise. Stressed on the second it is a verb meaning to grow.

questionText: Which is the CORRECT spelling of the word meaning both a light colour and to become faint?
explanation: Pale is correct - P-A-L-E. Pale is a homograph meaning a light colour and to become less impressive. Do not confuse with pail meaning a bucket.
